translationRepairs: Fahe said, "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; pluck too soon and it falls of itself.
Fahe said, "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; without plucking, it falls of itself.
不撩自落 means the fruit falls of itself without plucking; the original English reverses this into premature plucking.
Fahe said: "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; pluck too soon and it falls of itself.
Fahe said: "When mere men take fruit, they should wait until it is ripe; without plucking, it falls of itself.
Literal English repeats the same reversal of 不撩自落; without plucking is the correct sense.
Li's younger brother Zao was attendant cavalier, palace gentleman of the third rank, inspector of Xiang, Duke of Yixing county.
Li's younger brother Zao was attendant cavalier, Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, inspector of Xiang, and Duke of Yixing county.
儀同三司 is the honorific Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, not palace gentleman of the third rank.

Wenxuan feasted Fahe and his followers in Zhaoyang Hall, granting Fahe a million cash, a thousand lengths of goods, one first-grade mansion, a hundred qing of fields, two hundred slaves, living supplies and utensils in proportion; Song Li a thousand lengths; the rest from palace gentlemen of the third rank down to inspectors each had his difference.

其餘儀同、刺史以下 refers to holders of 儀同, not palace gentlemen of the third rank.

Wenxuan ordered the coffin opened and looked inside — only an empty coffin.
Chinese has 文宣; replacing idiomatic Gao Yang restores the temple name used in the source and the literal.
When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but court gentleman of the imperial law Huang Luohan and minister of the grand treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Chamberlain for Law Enforcement Huang Luohan and minister of the grand treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
廷尉卿 is Chamberlain for Law Enforcement, not court gentleman of the imperial law.
When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Court Gentleman of the Imperial Law Huang Luohan and Minister of the Grand Treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
When he arrived, the emperor had him sent down to the law; but Chamberlain for Law Enforcement Huang Luohan and Minister of the Grand Treasury Zhang Zai went to announce the decree to Lin's army.
廷尉卿 denotes the high judicial chamberlain; the proposed title is accurate.
Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said, "We beg Prince Lin enter the city — we will come out at once."
Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said, "We beg Young Master Wang enter the city — we will come out at once."
王郎 is a familiar honorific for Wang Lin (Young Master Wang), not the title Prince.
Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said: "We beg Prince Lin enter the city — we will come out at once."
Na and the rest cast down their weapons and bowed together; the whole army wept and said: "We beg Young Master Wang enter the city — we will come out at once."
王郎 does not mean Prince; Young Master Wang correctly renders the familiar address.
His friend master of documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him, "Lin has received your pull and lift; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.
His friend master of documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him, "Lin has received preferment; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.
拔擢 means preferment; the original invents second-person 'your pull and lift' absent from the Chinese.
His friend Master of Documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him: "Lin has received your pull and lift; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.
His friend Master of Documents Li Ying, whom the emperor favored — Lin told him: "Lin has received preferment; I have always wished to give my life to repay the state's grace.
拔擢 is preferment without stated addressee agency; preferment is the correct literal rendering.

Emperor Yuan, pressed by Wei siege, summoned Lin to the rescue and made him governor of Xiangzhou.
除湘州刺史 has no 再/又; removing 'again' restores fidelity to the source sentence.

Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisuipu.
白水浦 is the place-name Baisuipu; rendering it as a ford invents a geographic type the Chinese does not mark.

Lin then moved the Xiangzhou military headquarters to Yingcheng, with armor on a hundred thousand, drilling troops at Baisuipu.
白水浦 is Baisuipu as a place-name, not a ford; the proposed replacement is correct.

Wenxuan sent troops to escort him and also dispatched concurrent secretariat supervisor Li Taotu to invest Lin as Liang chancellor, commander of all armies within and without, and recorder of the masters of writing.
李騊駼 is Li Taotu, and the Chinese subject is 文宣; the proposal fixes the envoy name but still opens with Gao Yang, so both are corrected.

李騊駼 is standardly Li Taotu; Piaomo misreads the name, and the proposed literal is correct.
Attendant Yang Yin and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.
Attendant Yang Que and You Quanzhi and others carried imperial writs to proclaim favors in the Jiang region; from Lin downward all received gifts.
羊愨 is Yang Que, not Yang Yin; the proposed name matches the graph 愨.

羊愨 is Yang Que; the literal correctly replaces the misread Yin.

Chen sent Wu Mingche, inspector of Anzhou, up the Yangzi by night, intending a surprise on Pencheng.
湓城 is Pencheng, not Tuncheng; the proposed place-name matches the graph 湓.

He was appointed Inspector of Cangzhou; later Lin was made Specially Advanced and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
除 means to appoint, not remove; also 特進 is Specially Advanced, not Grand Mentor, so both errors are corrected.

驃騎 is Cavalry-General and 尚書僕射 is Vice Director; both corrections in the proposed literal are right.
From this speaking, there is indeed precedent to restrain us.
From this speaking, there is indeed such precedent.
抑有其例 uses 抑 as a classical particle meaning indeed, not the verb restrain.
